newsitem.title: USA: Mark IV to cut 1,000 jobs, take charge.
newsitem.headline: Mark IV to cut 1,000 jobs, take charge.

text.p: Mark IV Industries Inc. said Wednesday it will slash 1,000 jobs, or 6 percent of its workforce, as it shuts certain manufacturing and distribution facilities in the United States and Europe in an ongoing restructuring.
Mark IV said facilities that made power and fluid transfer systems and industrial and automotive components will start concentrating on one product line instead to improve efficiency.

The Amherst, N.Y.-based company expects to post a loss in the third quarter ending Nov. 30 as it takes an after-tax charge of about $66 million, or $1.04 per fully diluted share, to pay for the restructuring.
Of the $110 million in charges, pre-tax, some $60 million will be non-cash to account for the write-down of long-term assets.
Mark IV said it expects to realise pre-tax savings of between $40 million and $45 million per year, or 38 cents to 43 cents per share after taxes.

"The restructuring represents a major step forward in refocusing our operations to quickly and efficiently meet changing customer and competitive demands, while enabling the company to more fully employ its physical and human resources," said Sal H. Alfiero, chairman and CEO.

"It is essential that we become the low-cost producer in our various markets, regardless of where in the world we operate and whatever we manufacture. This restructuring effort continues our commitment to achieve this goal."
The closures affect all or part of 12 facilities in the United States and Europe.
Mark IV said it expects to meet analysts' earnings expectations of $1.65 to $1.70 per share for fiscal 1996 before the charges.
The company reported profits of $26.7 million, or 42 cents a share, on revenues of $577.1 million in the second quarter ended Aug. 31.
Mark IV's stock rose 87.5 cents to $22.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
